MISO S1073.evidence: A 75 MW surplus request by Big Rivers on the Hopkins to Reid 161 kV line, in service August 2026. It matches KYMEA Energy Center I, 75.2 MW of engines at Madisonville that connect through Big Rivers.

PJM AH1-721 - moved to TC2.evidence: East Kentucky Power Cooperative's 786 MW gas request on the Laurel to Cooper 161 kV line is the Cooper combined cycle unit, a GEM unit at Cooper power station.

PJM AH1-721.evidence: The same Cooper combined cycle request as the serial row, now in transition cycle 2. A GEM unit at Cooper power station.

PJM C01-1131.evidence: Kentucky Power's 479 MW gas request at Baker 345 kV in Lawrence County, in service September 2030. It matches the 480 MW of turbines in Kentucky Power's plan, which GEM holds as KPCO 2023 IRP power station.

PJM C01-1227.evidence: East Kentucky Power Cooperative's 780 MW gas request on the Spurlock to Meldahl Dam line in Mason County. Added as a new plant.

PJM C01-1228.evidence: East Kentucky Power Cooperative's 212 MW gas request on the Casey County to Liberty line is Liberty Station, a GEM plant under construction.

PJM C01-1325.evidence: Appalachian Power's 1,046 MW gas request at Baker 345 kV fits the combined cycle need in its 2025 resource plan, West Virginia case 25-0859-E-IRP, PDF pages 74 and 103, which GEM holds as two placeholders with guessed West Virginia points. Its 1,045 MW request C01-1326 in Wayne County, West Virginia is the other site option or the second plant.

TVA 417.evidence: TVA request 417, 780 MW of gas at the Paradise 500 kV station in Muhlenberg County, queued February 2020 with an in service date of October 2022, is the three Paradise combustion turbines, units 4, 5 and 6 at 250 MW each, already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for TVA 417.

TVA 55.evidence: TVA request 55, 640 MW in Marshall County, queued August 1999 and shown as operating with fuel listed as other, is the Marshall combustion turbine plant, eight 86 MW units already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for TVA 55.

TVA 628.evidence: TVA request 628, 1,600 MW of gas in Todd County on the Paradise to Montgomery 500 kV line, queued June 2024 with a 2030 in service date. No company is named. Staged as a new plant with owner blank. Sources: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for TVA 628, and the TVA transmission queue of January 2025 posted by WPLN.

TVA 657.evidence: TVA request 657 is a 60 MW increase at the Paradise combined cycle plant, project type Upgrade, due February 2030. It is an uprate of the existing unit, not a new unit. Staged as a question on Paradise CC1. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for TVA 657.

LGEE LGE-CS2025-002.evidence: LG&E request CS2025-002, 680 MW of gas at the Mill Creek 345 kV substation, is Mill Creek unit 6, 680 MW, already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-CS2025-002.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2022-003.evidence: LG&E request GIS-2022-003, 660 MW of gas at the Mill Creek 345 kV bus, is Mill Creek unit 5, the combined cycle under construction, already in GEM at 740 MW. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2022-003.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2023-002.evidence: KU request GIS-2023-002, 660 MW of gas at the Brown North 345 kV substation in Mercer County, is E.W. Brown unit 12, the planned combined cycle already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2023-002.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2024-002.evidence: Request GIS-2024-002, 75 MW of gas on the Madisonville to Earlington 69 kV line in Hopkins County, is KYMEA Energy Center I, 75.2 MW, already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2024-002.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2024-006.evidence: LG&E request GIS-2024-006, 94 MW of gas and oil at the Cane Run combustion turbine substation, agreement signed, in service May 2026. No filing names what it is. Staged as a question on Cane Run. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2024-006.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2010-001.evidence: LG&E request GIS-2010-001, 690 MW of gas at the Cane Run switching station, in service March 2015, is Cane Run unit 7, the combined cycle already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2010-001.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2013-001.evidence: LG&E request GIS-2013-001, 691 MW of gas and oil at the Cane Run switching station, in service March 2015, is a second request for Cane Run unit 7, already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2013-001.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2009-001.evidence: Request GIS-2009-001, 123 MW of gas in McCracken County on the Grahamville to South Paducah 161 kV line, in service May 2010, is the Paducah Power System plant, two 60 MW units from 2010, already in GEM. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2009-001.

LGEE LGE-GIS-2009-004.evidence: KU request GIS-2009-004, 785 MW at the Trimble County 345 kV substation, queued December 2009 with an in service date of October 2010, matches Trimble County unit 2, the coal unit that started in 2011, although the file lists the fuel as gas. The Trimble gas turbines are already in GEM. No new gas unit at Trimble is named in any filing. Source: Berkeley Lab Queued Up data file, tab 03. Complete Queue Data, row for LGE-GIS-2009-004.

us-ky:new:paducah-american-energy-hub-ga.evidence: The McCracken County GEM plants are Shawnee Fossil Plant, a TVA coal plant, and PPS power plant No 1, Paducah Power's 120 MW engine plant. Neither is NextEra's and neither is at the former gaseous diffusion plant site.

us-ky:new:ekpc-mason-county-gas-plant-pj.evidence: The only Mason County GEM plant is Spurlock power station, whose rows are the four coal units and their gas co-firing steps. The 780 MW request is a new plant; a question asks whether it belongs at Spurlock.

plan Big Rivers Electric Corporation.pages: All 565 PDF pages. Preferred plan: section 6.11.1 on PDF pages 281 to 282; action plan on PDF page 283; the other portfolios' new gas tables in sections 6.9 and 6.10 on PDF pages 251 to 280.

options.what: Retire the 65 MW Reid combustion turbine without replacing it (action plan item 1, PDF page 283)
Green Fuel Oil Backup Project, fuel oil backup for the two Sebree gas units (PDF pages 281 to 283)
The 635 MW gas plant from the 2023 plan is gone from the 2026 preferred plan
Other portfolios add 250 to 300 MW of F-frame combustion turbines and 150 to 500 MW of combined cycle when Green or Wilson retires (PDF pages 255 to 264). No site, year or company decision is named.
options.why_not: These are model results in portfolios the plan did not choose. No site is named, so there is nothing to add or watch.

plan Big Rivers Electric Corporation.evidence: Big Rivers' 2026 plan, filed September 29, 2026 in case 2026-00268, chooses the Model Optimization Reference Case portfolio (PDF page 281). It keeps Green and Wilson running, adds fuel oil backup at Green and builds no new gas unit. That drops the 635 MW plant from the 2023 plan, which GEM carries as BREC 2023 IRP power station; a question in this batch asks whether to cancel it. The action plan on PDF page 283 also asks the commission to retire the Reid turbine; the Reid and Green questions in this batch cover both.

plan Kentucky Power Company.pages: All 1,183 PDF pages of Volume A. Preferred plan: executive summary on PDF pages 13 to 16 and section on PDF pages 173 to 175; the combined cycle portfolio on PDF page 159.

additions.what: 480 MW of new gas combustion turbines in 2029 (PDF pages 15 and 175)

options.what: The combined cycle portfolio adds a 418 MW 1x1 combined cycle (PDF page 159). The utility's later certificate case 2026-00324 is a combined cycle in Lawrence County.

plan Kentucky Power Company.evidence: Kentucky Power's 2022 plan, filed March 20, 2023 in case 2023-00092, is still the newest; the next one is due March 2027. The preferred plan adds 480 MW of gas combustion turbines in 2029 (executive summary, PDF page 15). GEM has this as KPCO 2023 IRP power station. A question in this batch asks whether to fold that placeholder into the Lawrence County combined cycle in certificate case 2026-00324.

plan Duke Energy Kentucky.pages: All 160 PDF pages. Preferred plan: Figure 1.2 on PDF page 4; the alternative plans on PDF pages 5 to 11.

additions.what: East Bend unit 2 dual fuel conversion in 2029 (Figure 1.2, PDF page 4)
664 MW 1x1 combined cycle at East Bend from 2039 (Figure 1.2, PDF page 4)

options.what: 588 MW combined cycle with carbon capture at East Bend from 2036, in the plan without the federal carbon rule (Figure 1.3, PDF page 6)

plan Duke Energy Kentucky.evidence: Duke Energy Kentucky's 2024 plan, filed June 21, 2024 in case 2024-00197, is the newest. Case 2026-00167 only sets the date for the next one, due June 2027. Figure 1.2 on PDF page 4 shows East Bend running on coal and gas from 2029 and a 664 MW combined cycle from 2039; both are East Bend units in GEM. The 588 MW figure on PDF page 6 belongs to an alternative plan, so GEM's 664 MW stays. The Woodsdale turbines are in Ohio.

plan East Kentucky Power Cooperative.pages: All 245 PDF pages. Resource additions on PDF pages 26 to 27 (Figure 1) and the action plan from PDF page 27; certificate cases on PDF pages 156 to 161.

additions.what: Liberty engine plant, 214 MW, Casey County (case 2024-00310)
Gas co-firing at Spurlock units 1 to 4

plan East Kentucky Power Cooperative.evidence: East Kentucky Power Cooperative's 2025 plan, filed April 1, 2025 in case 2025-00087, puts every addition from its three certificate cases into the base case (PDF page 26): the 214 MW Liberty engine plant, the 745 MW Cooper combined cycle and gas co-firing at Spurlock 1 to 4 and Cooper 2. All are in GEM. Figure 1 on PDF page 27 shows no other new gas. The cooperative's PJM request at Spurlock is answered separately as EKPC Mason County gas plant.

plan Louisville Gas and Electric Company.pages: All 136 PDF pages of Volume I. Recommended plan: resource tables on PDF pages 114 to 115; summary on PDF pages 8 to 33.
plan Louisville Gas and Electric Company.evidence: The LG&E and KU 2024 plan, filed October 18, 2024 in case 2024-00326, is the newest; the next one is due October 2027. The tables on PDF pages 114 and 115 list Mill Creek 5 in 2027 and say the recommended plan adds combined cycle units in 2030 and 2031: Brown 12 and Mill Creek 6, both in GEM. No new simple cycle turbine is in the recommended plan.

plan Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency.pages: All 493 PDF pages. Preferred plan on PDF page 348; executive summary on PDF pages 11 to 37; the other plans, including Plan 4, on PDF pages 351 to 435; Section 16.2 on PDF pages 452 to 455.

additions.what: 75 MW engine plant, KYMEA Energy Center I (preferred plan, PDF page 348)

options.what: KYMEA Energy Center II, 92 MW (executive summary, PDF page 36)
Growing Energy Center I to 129 MW after 2029 (Section 16.2, PDF pages 452 to 455)

plan Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency.names_checked: KYMEA Energy Center II is not in GEM; it is a plan option, watched in us-ky:plant:monitor-4. 'Fossil Fuel-Fired Power Plant' on PDF page 263 is a rule title, not a site.
plan Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency.evidence: The Kentucky Municipal Energy Agency's IRP2023, approved by its board in January 2025, is posted on its own site, not filed with the commission. The preferred plan adds 75 MW of engines (PDF page 348); that is Energy Center I, in GEM at 75.2 MW and under construction. The plan also studies a 92 MW Energy Center II and an Energy Center I expansion to 129 MW. Neither is chosen, so both are watched.

plan Tennessee Valley Authority.pages: All 246 PDF pages of the final Volume 1. Table 4-1 on PDF page 105 (printed page 4-3) and the executive summary table on PDF page 14.

options.what: 4 to 13 GW of combined cycle and 3 to 13 GW of combustion turbines system-wide by 2050 (Table 4-1)
options.why_not: The plan names no site and no Kentucky plant. Projects come later as site-specific environmental reviews.

plan Tennessee Valley Authority.evidence: TVA's board approved the final 2026 plan in August 2026. Table 4-1 on PDF page 105 sets system-wide ranges for new gas: 4 to 13 gigawatts of combined cycle and 3 to 13 of combustion turbines. The plan names no site, in Kentucky or anywhere else. TVA's Kentucky gas projects come through its own environmental reviews.

plan Henderson Municipal Power & Light.pages: All 33 PDF pages. Table 5 on PDF page 23; portfolios on PDF pages 25 to 27; recommendations in section 6 on PDF pages 29 to 30.

options.what: 36 MW engine plant in 2030, recommended for development now (section 6, PDF pages 29 to 30)
79 MW share of a larger combustion turbine plant in 2036 (Table 5, PDF page 23)

plan Henderson Municipal Power & Light.evidence: Henderson Municipal Power and Light's 2026 plan, dated March 31, 2026, is not on its own site; a copy was posted by the Hendersonian in May 2026. Section 6 recommends starting development of a 36 MW engine plant for 2030 (PDF pages 29 to 30). That is under the 50 MW threshold, so it is watched in us-ky:plant:monitor-5 with the 2036 turbine share.
